dimensions.note: Second review. The blocking leak of the first review is closed: a Challenge's spec.token and spec.key and an Order's authorization tokens are blanked by value (`acmeSecrets`), trace names them for every level and seals the summary and the whole trace, and other objects are covered by shape (`keyAuthorizations`). Shown by running the parsers on cert-manager v1.20's two self-check texts and 25 variants. Read upstream at v1.20.0: acmeorders/sync.go never copies a Challenge reason or a problem document into an Order's reason, so the only verified road is the Challenge itself, which is blanked by value; Pebble v2.10.1 quotes the expected key authorization only for HTTP-01 and no DNS-01 digest. Not blocking, what is left: (1) the shape finder in `_helpers.ts` lines 75-76 misses a key authorization that is directly followed by a dot and a letter (`<key>.Retry`), directly preceded by a dot, cut short, or broken by a line break, and the URL finder misses a percent-encoded path; the README names the bare token and the DNS-01 value as limits but not these. None is a text cert-manager v1.20 is known to write. (2) `seal` leaves a fixed list of identity fields and blanks every other text, so a value an ACME server chooses can blank a field a workflow compares: a spec.key of `processing` turns the Challenge's `state` into `[redacted]`, and a token of `challenge` would turn a trace's `stage` into a value its schema refuses. It needs a hostile ACME server; sealing only message fields (reason, message, summary, readyMessage, issuingMessage, error, pollError) would end it. (3) README 'What is never stored' says 'no ACME URL': true for fields, but a message may quote one (an HTTP-01 challenge URL is kept with its token blanked). Unchanged and checked again: no CSR, certificate or CA body, solver configuration or account detail is copied; no Secret is read; the patch body is on standard input only.

Entry and completion at info with structured placeholders. The trace summary that is logged is built from sealed levels and sealed again; a unit test and smoke batch C look for the key authorization in it.

The three points of the first review are fixed: a Certificate deleted during the poll is outcome `deleted` with only the renewal record; a patch with no usable answer says the renewal may have been triggered; a missing object is told by kind not-found. Cutting a patch error at the first `{` keeps the server's sentence for every refusal checked (Forbidden, Conflict, NotFound, Unauthorized, invalid field paths, unknown flag); only the quoted value after it is lost. Notes: a connection that was refused is also reported as 'may have been triggered', which is cautious, not wrong; a run cancelled while the patch is out ends as a plain Error, not as a cancelled kind; `patchSaid` blanks every text of 8 or more characters the patch held, so a condition reason that is also a word of kubectl's sentence would be blanked there.

84 unit tests pass; the fake now really repeats the patch body, and the key authorization has fixtures for both self-check texts, a trace, the inventory lines and a live case (`acme-test/wrong`, batches B, C, G). Left: (1) that the API server refuses a merge patch with a stale metadata.resourceVersion on the status subresource is still shown on the fake only. The README and smoke/README now say so, but a direct `kubectl patch --subresource=status` with an old resourceVersion in batch D would show the server's side without any hook. (2) No test holds the shapes the finder misses (see credentials). (3) The self-check text that quotes the challenge URL is a unit fixture only; smoke shows the `expected "..."` text. smoke/README says no log of the run is kept, so the live results cannot be checked by a reader.

As in the first review: read, refuse a True Issuing condition, patch bound to the resourceVersion read, answer checked; a second run after an unknown outcome is refused as already issuing. A Certificate without a status gets conditions [Issuing] only.

The condition matches cmctl renew; the outcome follows what cert-manager does with Issuing on success and failure. Lists and single objects are checked for kind, name and namespace. lastTransitionTime is the operator machine's clock, as with cmctl.

Every kubectl call has a request timeout and is stopped 5 s later; the poll is bounded by waitSeconds (at most 120) and counts read time. The new upper bound on a time limit in lib/cli.ts does not touch any call here (35 s).

Placeholder names and example.org / example.test only. The README states the limits of the blanking, the data-name collision and what is shown on the fake only. One wording: 'no ACME URL' holds for fields, not for quoted messages.

Plain z.object, no passthrough; a test pins that every record has exactly its schema's fields. The new outcome `deleted` is in the enum and its description. Minor, as before: Date.parse accepts more than RFC 3339. See credentials (2) for the one way a sealed value can leave an enum.
Read-only types plus one action; nothing is created or deleted.
kubectl-cli-available, labelled live, on all five types; renew's own checks run before the write.

Both points of the first review are answered: an issuer list narrowed to one kind writes no inventory (tested), and the README says that get, trace and renew cannot see a second object of the same data name when a name or namespace holds `--`.
